name: User-assigned device name
plain: Reads the name the person gave their phone: free on Android, locked to a generic name on iOS 16 and later.
meaning: A name like Jane's iPhone leaks a real name and maybe a family. Apple stopped this in iOS 16; Android still shows it.

android.api_surface: Settings.Global.DEVICE_NAME (API 25); BluetoothAdapter.getName() needs BLUETOOTH_CONNECT on Android 12+
android.note: Often the model name by default

ios.api_surface: Returns a generic iPhone since iOS 16 unless Apple approves the entitlement (managed or enterprise cases)

fields.name: name
fields.range: free text up to about 32 chars

limits.headline: Can see the name you gave your phone on Android, but a generic one on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing on Android. The app checks when it starts
can: See the phone name you set on Android, often just the model by default
See the Bluetooth name on Android 12 and newer, if you allow Nearby devices
Show your name in a welcome or pairing screen
cannot: See your custom name on iPhone 16 and newer; apps only get a generic iPhone name
Get your real iPhone name unless Apple approves an entitlement for a managed or business app
See the Bluetooth name on Android 12 and newer without the Nearby devices permission
limits.differs: Android shares the name by default. iPhone hides it from apps since iOS 16 unless Apple approves a special case.

story.what_it_is: The name you gave your phone, like Jane's iPhone.

marketing.name: User assigned device name entitlement
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps need a special Apple approved entitlement to read the name a person gave their device.

story.for_you: If your phone is called Jane's Pixel, any Android app can read that. On iPhone, apps see only a generic name like iPhone. Rename your phone to remove your name from the open.
story.for_makers: A real name is a strong ID. Makers can use it to greet you, show device lists and pair devices. Ad and data firms can use it to link a phone to a real person.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows 'Jane's Pixel' in your list of signed in devices, so you can spot a stranger.
A smart home app pairs with a speaker and lists phones by the names you gave them.
A local multiplayer game shows each player's phone name in the lobby.
A data firm reads the name to guess a first and last name for a profile.
A bank shows trusted devices by name so you can remove an old one.
A file sharing app lists nearby phones by their names.

story.android_note: Readable with no prompt on Android, though newer versions limit it more.
story.ios_note: Locked to a generic name since iOS 16 unless the app has an Apple approved entitlement.

technical_bounds: iOS: entitlement only for approved cases

history.change: UIDevice.name returns generic device name without entitlement
